Give It a Life

I like to see it lap the Miles

Emily Dickinson (first published 1891)

I like to see it lap the Miles —
And lick the Valleys up —
And stop to feed itself at Tanks —
And then — prodigious step

Around a Pile of Mountains —
And supercilious peer
In Shanties — by the sides of Roads —
And then a Quarry pare

To fit its Ribs
And crawl between
Complaining all the while
In horrid — hooting stanza —
Then chase itself down Hill —

And [a:neigh] like Boanerges —
Then — prompter than a Star
Stop — docile and omnipotent
At its own [a:stable] door —
  • lap = drink with the tongue · Tanks = water tanks that refill a steam train
  • prodigious = huge, amazing · supercilious = looking down proudly
  • Shanties = rough little huts · Quarry = a pit where stone is cut · pare = cut away
  • horrid = awful · Boanerges = “sons of thunder”, a very loud voice
  • prompter = quicker, more on time · docile = gentle, obedient · omnipotent = all-powerful
